task: Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once. Reach the goal.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: 'Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once' is correctly a hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost) — key_lost (a drop while the door is shut) may not occur before the first door_open, and the ban lifts after that first opening, exactly as the 'until' wording demands — and 'Reach the goal' is the hard Existence(at_goal), so FINAL_STATES is nonempty. Both clauses trace to task sentences with hard priorities matching the wording; no clause is added or redundant. Opening the door is not commanded by the task (it appears only as the 'until' condition), so no Existence(door_open) is required — the environment already guarantees at_goal implies door_open.
